source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Only five of New Jersey's 48 mapped data centers publish power figures, and CyrusOne's Somerset campus is 20.7 percent of that disclosed total at 23 MW.

That share is a statement about disclosure, not about the state's data center fleet. The five operators that publish total 111.3 MW, and the other 43 mapped facilities contribute nothing to that number because their consumption is not published. Somerset ranks second in New Jersey by published IT capacity, behind one larger facility, but the ranking is drawn from a denominator that omits most of the state.

The 23 MW sits across 185,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack that floor area supports roughly 575 racks, and at 80 kW per rack roughly 290. The same building therefore holds either a conventional colocation footprint or a denser AI training configuration, and the published data does not say which. Power, not square footage, is what determines how much compute a facility can host, and 23 MW is modest against hyperscale AI clusters.

What the data does not cover is decisive. The campus publishes no certifications qualifying it for specific workloads, no tenant base, and no actual consumption profile, so nothing here establishes whether AI workloads run in Somerset at all. The suitability score of 64 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion missing. Proximity to the New York metro market is the one geographic fact present, and it is not by itself evidence of AI relevance.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
